newsitem.title: HONG KONG: C&W positioned to revive stalled China talks-paper.
newsitem.headline: C&W positioned to revive stalled China talks-paper.

text.p: Cable and Wireless Plc was positioned to revive stalled business projects in China after its deal to sell a slice of unit Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd to China Telecom, a newspaper reported on Sunday.
The Sunday Morning Post said Cable & Wireless (C&W) would revive talks with China for a mobile phone network in Beijing and the building of a Hong Kong-Beijing fibre-optic link.

The British telecommunications giant was expected to enjoy new leverage in business dealings with China after it sold a 5.5 percent, or US$1.185 billion, stake in HongKong Telecom to state-owned China Telecom, the paper quoted sources as saying.
The sale cuts C&W's previous 59.2 percent share in HongKong Telecom to 53.7 percent.
China Telecom is controlled by Telpo Communications Development Ltd, a holding company of China's Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications.
The unidentified sources were also quoted as saying work on the fibre-optic link had begun, but talks on the mobile phone network, which go back to at least 1994, were continuing.

C&W said it might transfer more shares in HongKong Telecom to China -- with a view to both China Telecom and C&W becoming equal shareholders -- but only if such a move enhanced shareholder value and if "important projects in mainland China" were realised.
